key_insight: Specialized continued pretraining for materials science (LLaMat) enables smaller, purpose-built LLMs to outperform larger general-purpose models; heavily pretrained models (e.g., LLaMA-3) adapt less effectively to new scientific domains than their less-extensively pretrained counterparts.
problem_solved: How to build cost-effective, high-performing language models for materials research and whether extensive prior pretraining helps or hinders domain adaptation during continued pretraining.
method: Create a family of domain-adapted LLMs (LLaMat) at multiple sizes via continued pretraining on materials-science corpora.
Compare adaptation and downstream performance of LLaMat variants against general LLMs (LLaMA-2, LLaMA-3) across materials-specific benchmarks.
Analyze how pretraining extent affects adaptability, showing that more extensively pretrained models can be less flexible when continued-pretrained on new scientific data.
impact: Guides practitioners to prefer targeted continued pretraining of compact models for scientific domains, achieving better performance and lower cost than blindly scaling general LLMs; signals caution when adapting very extensively pretrained models.
visual_elements: Performance vs model size plot showing LLaMat small/medium models outperforming larger general LLMs on materials tasks

paper_title: A family of large language models for materials research with insights into model adaptability in continued pretraining
paper_authors: Dhruv Ahlawat, Vaibhav Mishra, Somaditya Singh, Mohd Zaki, Vaibhav Bihani
